senses.gloss:
nāḍīśuddhi
(‘purification of the nāḍīs’)
------------------------------------------
Nāḍīśuddhi means the purification of the nāḍīs, tube-like structures in the body. They have to be cleansed by certain processes before practising प्राणायाम. (See PRĀṆĀYĀMA.)
Works on हठयोग describe nāḍī-शुद्धि as of two types: समनु (with bījamantras) and nirmanu (without such mantras).
The latter is done by practising various dhautis (cleansing processes). (See DHAUTI for details.)
The former is the usual प्राणायाम comprising the three stages, पूरक (inhalation), कुम्भक (retention of breath) and रेचक (exhalation) in the proportion of 16:64:32 seconds, using such bījamantras as yaṁ, raṁ and laṁ (vide Gheraṇḍa Saṁhitā 5.33-45).
Of course, it goes without saying that these practices should be done under the direct supervision of a competent गुरु.
